secretstore.source.reportWhat: Where this service reads its primordial secrets from — the key-encryption key everything it seals is sealed under, and the database password — whether it actually read them, and what the store at the other end is doing.
secretstore.source.wrapsInKms: each data encryption key, in the KMS
secretstore.source.wrapsInVault: each data encryption key, in the vault
secretstore.source.fileNotObject: The file is not a JSON object, so whatever is in it is taken whole. That is what a raw key file is.
secretstore.source.memberNames: Member NAMES only. Which one a secret takes is its own field setting.
secretstore.source.noField: No field is configured, so the whole file is this secret.
secretstore.source.sharesKekFile: This secret shares the key-encryption key's file and that file is not a JSON object — so what is in it is the KEY, and reading this secret is REFUSED rather than handing that key to a database.
secretstore.source.fileNotJson: The file is not JSON, so the whole of it is this secret and the field is not used.
secretstore.source.noLogin: No client certificate is configured, so no login was made: the token is whatever {{token}} or the SDK's VAULT_TOKEN supplies.
secretstore.source.canWrite: THIS IDENTITY CAN WRITE. It could replace the key-encryption key, and everything sealed under the old one would be unreadable.
secretstore.source.readOnly: Read-only on every path it was asked about, which is what the policy is supposed to say.
secretstore.source.reachesNothing: This identity may not reach any of the paths it is configured to read. A read at startup would be refused.

secretstore.probe.file/file: The file itself: whether it is there, who can read it, and when it last changed.
secretstore.probe.file/members: Whether the file holds a JSON object, and which members are in it — the NAMES and never the values.
secretstore.probe.file/field: Whether the member this secret is configured to take is actually in the file.
secretstore.probe.vault/client-certifica: The certificate this service presents to the store, and when it expires.
secretstore.probe.vault/store-ca: The anchor this service verifies the store's own listener against.
secretstore.probe.vault/seal-status: Whether the store is initialised, whether it is sealed, what kind of seal it has, and which build it is.
secretstore.probe.vault/health: The store's own health summary: its clock, its cluster, and whether this node is the active one.
secretstore.probe.vault/leader: High availability: whether this node is the leader, and where the leader is.
secretstore.probe.vault/authentication: Logging in the way a startup read does, and what the store handed back.
secretstore.probe.vault/token: What the store says about the token that login produced, asked of the store rather than read off the login reply.
secretstore.probe.vault/capabilities: What this identity may actually do, asked of the store: the paths it reads, and a write it must not be able to make.
secretstore.probe.vault/mounts: The secret engines this identity can see — which is fewer than the store has, and should be.
secretstore.probe.vault/versions: The KV metadata for this secret: when it was written, how many versions there are, and which one a read gets.
secretstore.probe.aws/describe: Everything AWS Secrets Manager knows about this secret EXCEPT its value: rotation, the KMS key, the versions and their staging labels.
secretstore.probe.vault-transit/transit-: What Transit says about the key that wraps the data keys: its type, its versions, and whether it may ever leave the KMS.
secretstore.probe.aws-kms/kms-key: What AWS KMS says about the key that wraps the data keys: its state and whether AWS rotates it.
secretstore.probe.gcp-kms/kms-key: What Cloud KMS says about the key that wraps the data keys: its purpose, its primary version and its rotation schedule.
secretstore.probe.azure-keys/vault-key: What the vault says about the key that wraps the data keys: its type, size, operations, version and rotation.
secretstore.probe.gcp/secret: The secret's own metadata: replication, labels, rotation and expiry.
secretstore.probe.gcp/version: The version a read would get: whether it is enabled, disabled or destroyed.
secretstore.probe.azure/versions: Every version of this secret and its properties — enabled, created, updated, expiry — and never the value.
